Area.evidence_source: ['[page/7/Text/7] Prevailing across the unforeseen and rationalized cases were participants\' actions toward managing their emotions. Often touched upon were men\'s shock, guilt, and/or regret in detailing that they wished they had been able to alter the outcome. However, most participants managed their emotions by detaching themselves from the suicide amid detailing their commitment to avoiding a similar fate.', '[page/8/Text/4] I think women have more of an emotional literacy because it\'s something that\'s modelled and encouraged from a young age . . . it\'s more comfortable for them. I think men experience emotion as deep as women, but have a harder time identifying it for themselves and relating it to other people, and then it becomes an isolating thing . . . I think talking about sadness is saying like, "I don\'t have it figured out, I\'m not in control." I think men . . . really try to keep the lid on it . . . I try to keep the lid on a lot. I think I\'m more than your average emotional male as far as communication, but I still keep a hell of a lot under there.', '[page/8/Text/9] I\'ve got a wife and kids and my wellbeing is not just about myself anymore so I have to be responsible to them and the result of that is I have to suck it up and not be prideful about getting help. And if I have a health or mental issue that I need some help with, get it taken care of because I need to be there not only for myself but for other people.', '[page/8/Text/12] Participants\' commitment to being healthy and open to receiving help when necessary was also positioned as protective against suicide.']
